q: On 10 October 2025, a divisional accounts clerk is checking a coaching earnings statement for AC Chair Car tickets with a taxable value of Rs 2,000 per ticket. Which GST rate should be applied under GST 2.0?

A passenger travels in an ordinary non-AC second class coach after GST 2.0 came into force. A trainee proposes to charge GST at 5% on the fare, treating it like AC travel. What is the correct position?

options.B: GST at 18% is payable
options.C: The service is exempt from GST

q: A bill clerk suggests that the Railways should account for GST on their own goods freight traffic under Reverse Charge, arguing that transportation of goods is a service. What should Accounts advise?

options.A: The freight customer must pay the tax under RCM in every case
options.B: The Railways' own freight service is under forward charge; the Railways issue the invoice and pay the tax
options.C: The suggestion is correct and RCM applies to railway freight
options.D: No GST is payable on railway freight at all

q: A zonal railway pays a supplier under a works contract. The total value of supply under the contract is Rs 8,00,000, and the invoice shows GST separately. The bill section must decide on GST-TDS. Which treatment is correct?

options.A: GST-TDS at 2% on the value excluding GST shown on the invoice
options.B: No GST-TDS, because income-tax TDS alone applies to works bills
options.C: GST-TDS at 18% on the total invoice value including GST
options.D: GST-TDS at 5% on the value excluding GST

q: The Railways receive a supply that is notified under Reverse Charge from an unregistered supplier. The receiving office asks how the tax is to be paid and accounted for. Which sequence is correct?

options.A: Supplier issues a tax invoice, charges GST, and the Railways take ITC without payment
options.B: The Railways raise a self-invoice, pay the tax in cash through the electronic cash ledger, and then take ITC if eligible
options.C: The Railways pay the tax by using ITC in the electronic credit ledger
options.D: No invoice or payment is needed because the supplier is unregistered

q: In IPAS, GST paid on a works-contract for construction of an office building is flagged as a restricted credit. A clerk proposes to claim full ITC because the tax was actually paid to the contractor. What is the correct position?

options.A: ITC is available because the tax was actually paid
options.B: ITC is available if the contractor files his return
options.C: ITC is blocked under Section 17(5) for works-contract / construction of immovable property such as buildings and bridges
options.D: ITC is available at 50% for civil structures

q: A supplier covered by e-invoicing issues a B2B invoice but does not report it to the Invoice Registration Portal. The railway buyer asks whether ITC can safely be taken on that invoice. What is the correct advice?

options.A: An unreported invoice of a covered taxpayer is not treated as an invoice at all, and the buyer's ITC is at risk
options.B: ITC is safe because e-invoicing is only an optional formality
options.C: ITC is safe if the supplier gives a written undertaking
options.D: The invoice becomes valid automatically after 30 days

q: GST rates are reduced while a railway supply contract is running, and the contractor continues to bill at the old contract price without passing on the benefit. Which principle is attracted in tender finalisation and contract working?

options.A: The contractor may retain the benefit as additional profit
options.B: The matter is governed only by income-tax TDS rules
options.C: The Railways must increase the contract price proportionately
options.D: The anti-profiteering principle: a rate reduction or additional ITC benefit must be passed on to the recipient by a commensurate reduction in prices

q: Consider the following statements about the GST 2.0 rate structure: I. The merit rate is 5%. II. The standard rate is 18%. III. A special rate of 40% applies to sin / demerit and luxury goods. IV. The 12% and 28% slabs continue as the two principal slabs. Which of the statements given above are correct?

options.B: I, II and III only

q: Consider the following statements about the conditions for claiming Input Tax Credit: I. The buyer must hold a valid tax invoice or debit note. II. The supplier must have reported the supply so that it reflects in the buyer's auto-drafted ITC statement. III. The buyer must have received the goods or services and filed his return. IV. The tax must actually have been paid by the supplier to the Government. Which of the statements given above are correct?

options.B: II and IV only

q: Consider the following statements about Reverse Charge Mechanism: I. Under RCM, the liability to pay tax shifts from the supplier to the recipient. II. The recipient must raise a self-invoice for an RCM supply. III. RCM liability must be paid in cash through the electronic cash ledger. IV. The Railways' own freight transportation service is charged under RCM. Which of the statements given above are correct?

options.B: I and IV only

q: Consider the following statements about place of supply for transport services: I. For transport of passengers, where the recipient is registered, the place of supply is the location of the recipient. II. For transport of passengers, where the passenger is unregistered, the place of supply is the place where the passenger embarks for a continuous journey. III. For transport of goods to an unregistered recipient, the place of supply is the place where the goods are handed over for transportation. Which of the statements given above are correct?

options.B: II only

q: Consider the following statements about the e-way bill: I. An e-way bill is required for movement of goods of consignment value exceeding Rs 50,000. II. It is generated on the basis of documents such as a tax invoice, bill of supply or delivery note. III. Its validity is linked to the distance to be travelled. IV. It is required only when goods are exported out of India. Which of the statements given above are correct?

options.B: I, II and III only

q: Consider the following statements about taxes subsumed under GST: I. Central excise duty was subsumed in GST. II. Service tax and VAT were subsumed in GST. III. Income tax was subsumed in GST and no longer continues separately. IV. Professional tax, a local levy, continues. Which of the statements given above are correct?

options.B: III only

q: GST 2.0, the rate rationalisation decided by the 56th GST Council, came into effect from:

options.B: 1 July 2017

q: GST-TDS on payments by government departments and other notified deductors is provided under which section of the CGST Act?

options.B: Section 17(5)

q: The GST-TDS deducted under Section 51 of the CGST Act is deposited and reported by the deductor through which return?

options.B: GSTR-7

q: Under e-invoicing, the Invoice Registration Portal (IRP) returns which of the following to the supplier on reporting a B2B invoice?

options.A: A Goods Receipt Note and a challan number
options.B: A TAN and a PAN reference
options.D: An Invoice Reference Number (IRN) and a signed QR code

q: A dealer opting for the Composition Scheme under GST issues which document instead of a tax invoice?

options.B: A tax invoice with tax collected separately

q: In the 15-character GSTIN of a tax deductor, the 14th character is denoted by which letter?

options.B: G

options.A: The 40% slab is the standard rate for most goods and services
options.B: The old 12% and 28% slabs have been removed
options.C: Exempt supplies, such as non-AC passenger transport by rail, continue at 0% / exempt

q: Which of the following statements about blocked Input Tax Credit is NOT correct?

options.A: ITC is blocked on motor vehicles and conveyances except for prescribed uses
options.B: ITC is blocked on goods lost, stolen, destroyed or written off
options.C: ITC is blocked on food, outdoor catering and personal-use items except where obligatory
options.D: ITC is freely available on works-contract for construction of buildings and bridges because the tax is paid to the contractor

q: Which of the following statements about Tax Collected at Source under GST is NOT correct?

options.A: The Railways, as payer on their works bills, collect TCS under Section 52 of the CGST Act
options.B: TCS under GST is collected by electronic commerce operators on supplies made through their platform
options.C: The e-commerce operator files GSTR-8 for TCS
options.D: The seller claims credit for the TCS collected by the operator

q: Which of the following statements about place and time of supply is NOT correct?

options.A: On an intra-State supply, CGST plus SGST/UTGST are charged
options.B: On an inter-State supply, IGST is charged
options.C: For services, time of supply is always the last day of the financial year, regardless of invoice or payment
options.D: GST is a destination-based tax, so revenue accrues to the State where the supply is consumed

q: Which of the following statements about advances and deposits under GST is NOT correct?

options.A: GST is leviable on advances received for services
options.B: A mere deposit is taxed immediately on receipt, even before it is utilised towards any supply
options.C: GST is not leviable on advances received for goods
options.D: A penalty adjusted out of a security deposit becomes taxable when it is actually utilised towards a supply

q: Which of the following statements about the Composition Scheme is NOT correct?

options.A: It is a simplified levy with minimal compliance for small suppliers up to the prescribed turnover limit
options.B: A composition dealer issues a Bill of Supply, not a tax invoice
options.C: A composition dealer cannot collect tax from the buyer
options.D: A composition dealer can collect tax separately on the invoice and claim full ITC on purchases

q: Which of the following statements about GST returns and railway accounting systems is NOT correct?

options.A: GSTR-9 is the monthly summary return used for periodical payment of GST
options.B: Periodical payment of GST is made through the summary return GSTR-3B
options.C: Input taxes paid on the Railways are tracked through reports generated in AIMS (IPAS)

q: Which of the following statements about exempt railway-related supplies and incidental charges is NOT correct?

options.A: Exempt supplies earn no ITC, and credit on inputs used for exempt outputs must be reversed proportionately
options.B: Detention charges for loading and unloading, forming part of the consideration, take the GST treatment of the main supply
options.C: Services of leasing of rolling-stock assets by IRFC to Indian Railways are taxable at the standard rate of 18%
options.D: A tax invoice shows the taxable value, the GST and the total invoice value

q: Which of the following statements about utilisation of Input Tax Credit is NOT correct?

options.A: IGST credit is used first in the prescribed cross-utilisation order
options.B: CGST credit can be freely set off against SGST liability, and SGST credit against CGST liability
options.C: Where ITC is available on a stores purchase, the material is costed excluding the creditable GST
options.D: Where inputs serve both taxable and exempt purposes, credit is restricted to the taxable, business portion

q: Assertion (A): GST is a destination-based consumption tax. Reason (R): Revenue under GST accrues to the State where the supply is consumed, not where it originates.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

q: Assertion (A): The Railways charge GST on their own freight transportation service under forward charge. Reason (R): RCM applies to railway freight because transportation of goods is a service.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

q: Assertion (A): Where a stores item is purchased and ITC is available on it, the GST amount is not treated as part of the cost in the priced accounts. Reason (R): The GST Council is constituted under Article 279A of the Constitution and is chaired by the Union Finance Minister.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

q: Assertion (A): GST-TDS under Section 51 of the CGST Act is deducted at 5% of the contract payment. Reason (R): Amounts recovered as GST-TDS but not remitted to the Government attract interest at 18% per annum.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

q: Assertion (A): A B2B invoice of an e-invoicing-covered taxpayer that is not reported to the IRP is not treated as an invoice at all. Reason (R): E-invoicing imposes a new tax in addition to GST on the same supply.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

q: Match the railway supply (I-IV) with its GST position under GST 2.0 (a-d): I. AC passenger classes including First Class II. Other taxable services generally III. Sin / demerit and luxury goods IV. Non-AC ordinary passenger classes a. 18% b. Exempt c. 5% d. 40%

options.B: I-a, II-c, III-d, IV-b

q: Match the GST return (I-IV) with its purpose (a-d): I. GSTR-3B II. GSTR-9 III. GSTR-7 IV. GSTR-8 a. TCS return filed by the e-commerce operator b. GST-TDS return filed by the deductor c. Annual return d. Summary return for periodical payment

options.B: I-c, II-d, III-b, IV-a

q: Match the ITC category flagged in IPAS (I-IV) with its description (a-d): I. Non-business activity II. Exempt supplies III. Restricted credits IV. Partially eligible credits a. Credit blocked under Section 17(5), such as civil-structure expenditure b. Credit worked out in the proportion of taxable supplies to total supplies c. Inputs used for supplies that earn no ITC d. Inputs used for activities outside business use

options.B: I-d, II-c, III-a, IV-b

q: Match the supply situation (I-IV) with its tax treatment or place of supply (a-d): I. Supplier location and place of supply are in the same State II. Supplier location and place of supply are in different States III. Transport of goods to an unregistered recipient - place of supply IV. Transport of an unregistered passenger - place of supply a. IGST is charged b. Place where the goods are handed over for transportation c. CGST plus SGST/UTGST are charged d. Place where the passenger embarks for a continuous journey

options.B: I-c, II-a, III-b, IV-d

q: Match the workflow element (I-IV) with its function (a-d): I. Invoice Registration Portal II. E-way bill III. AIMS (IPAS) reports IV. Party Master a. Source of the correct GSTIN of the supplier for GST-TDS credit b. Tracking of input taxes paid on the Railways c. Registration of a B2B invoice, returning IRN and QR code d. Document required for movement of goods above the prescribed value

options.B: I-d, II-c, III-b, IV-a

q: Match the provision (I-IV) with the subject it governs (a-d): I. Section 51, CGST Act II. Section 52, CGST Act III. Section 9(3), CGST Act IV. Section 17(5), CGST Act a. Reverse Charge on notified supplies b. Blocked Input Tax Credit c. GST-TDS by notified deductors d. TCS by e-commerce operators

options.B: I-c, II-a, III-d, IV-b
